supported_observations: Shared foreground process group causes parent shell job control to treat supervisor stop as foreground-job return.
Bash early READY and dash RETURN:148 are consistent with the outer controller consuming a stopped helper status, not supervisor-internal main completion.
The supervisor already distinguishes stop/continue through WUNTRACED and WCONTINUED; numeric 148 special-casing would conflate exit 148 with SIGTSTP.
Parent WAIT native SIGTSTP is ignored in the observed interactive PTY session and must be tested as no-op without prompt or stale-input escape rather than forced to stop.
minimal_fix_direction: Keep the same persistent parent and same terminal session, but separate supervisor PG_S from experiment PG_E.
Keep the supervisor observable; make only PG_E the foreground process group and native TSTP target.
Before SIGCONT, the same-session supervisor blocks SIGTTOU, restores foreground ownership with tcsetpgrp, verifies tcgetpgrp, then continues PG_E.
Treat STOPPED and CONTINUED as live states that cannot emit MAIN_RETURN, lifetime completion, input release, or parent control return.
When no experiment target exists, record NO_TARGET; do not infer experiment suspension from a supervisor signal marker.
discriminating_experiment: Run Bash/dash shared-PG negative control versus split-PG candidate with a prepared child barrier, real PTY Ctrl-Z, WIFSTOPPED and /proc T plus supervisor PING, foreground restore before SIGCONT, resumed acknowledgement, main-return with live setsid descendant, input barrier, stale writer, and same-parent prompt/new input. Bound and clean every owned PG/PID.
regression_test_ideas: repeat stop/continue and failed foreground restoration
Ctrl-C no tail and Bash/dash SIGQUIT differences
return/exec/setsid descendants and input-return stale marker
integration_risks: Background helper launch can redirect stdin unless PTY ownership is explicit.
A child-handler installation race before foreground transfer can still expose parent job control.
setsid descendants remain a lifetime-tracking concern but cannot receive terminal Ctrl-Z as the former experiment PG.
remaining_unknowns: Whether the split-PG candidate preserves the full Bash/dash input-return and descendant-lifetime sequence.
Whether parent control latch or another trap path still returns READY after process-group separation.
